paper.title: ARISE: Agent Reasoning with Intrinsic Skill Evolution in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
paper.central_claim: ARISE: a hierarchical RL framework where a shared policy is both Skills Manager and Worker; it selects skills by log-prob scoring, distills successful traces into a two-tier skill library, and a hierarchical reward co-evolves reasoning and library; outperforms GRPO-family and memory-augmented baselines, especially out of distribution, and each component contributes.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref=null: claude-kimi worker run, no per-call receipt exposed to the worker; model type per template (haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]). Baseline named in text (SkillRL) has no row in Table 1.

sections_read: App.E (sensitivity, library evolution, phases, token/compute cost)

rationale: 技能库与策略联训，数学基准较GRPO约+1.8~3.5分；但选择/生成动作无梯度、无方差、AIME24调参、缺外部检索器与记忆开关对照，留存因果弱。

evidence.quote: a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework in which a shared policy operates both as a high-level Skills Manager and a low-level Worker
evidence.support_explanation: Central system claim: one shared policy manages skill selection/generation and solves tasks.

evidence.quote: skill management, including both skill selection before execution and skill summarization after execution, is delegated to an external retriever, preventing the policy gradient from directly shaping skill selection.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap 1: external retriever decoupled from the policy gradient.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, the skill library is updated independently of the RL objective, breaking the feedback loop between policy improvement and library enrichment
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap 2: library updated independently of RL.

evidence.quote: govern both selection and generation, the advantage signal from the hierarchical reward propagates end-to-end through the selection mechanism.
evidence.support_explanation: Mechanism claim that the policy gradient shapes selection.

evidence.quote: The policy is updated via the clipped surrogate objective:
evidence.support_explanation: Eq.6 is a per-token ratio over solution-trajectory tokens x_{i,l} of the G rollouts only; there is no term for the selection draw z_t or for the O_{G+1} skill-generation tokens, so the 'end-to-end' claim in E004 is not carried by the written loss (our reading of Eq.5-6, App.A.2 step 7).

evidence.quote: and the importance sampling ratio now reflects skill-conditioned generation:
evidence.support_explanation: Phase II ratio conditions solution tokens on the injected skill; gradient reaches selection only indirectly through shared parameters.

evidence.support_explanation: Greedy decoding (temperature 0) makes the 32 'independent runs' near-identical, so they do not estimate variance.

signatures.object: Tiered skill library: cache (Cc=10) + reservoir (Cr=100) of 220-char JSON skill documents (name, problem_type, key_insight, 2-3 method steps, check), each with EMA utility
signatures.information: Query + positive-advantage solution traces (<=2, clipped 400 chars) from the same GRPO group, ground-truth correctness reward; no access to test problems
signatures.operation: Dedicated rollout O_{G+1} by the same policy summarizes successes into one skill; four-stage format validation; Add -> Evict/Load/Delete by utility
signatures.output: Updated cache/reservoir; fallback 'trace_abstract' skill if JSON invalid (<15% of attempts after warm-up)
signatures.feedback: r_task correctness and r_skill bonus -> hierarchical reward R in {0,1,2}; utility u<-0.9u+0.1R for selected skill
signatures.selection_rule_data: Admission = format validity only (no marginal-gain/regression test); retention = lowest-utility eviction, reservoir deletion if bottom-10% utility and zero usage; utility is raw reward EMA (confounded by difficulty per App.D.3)
signatures.persistence: Library persists across training steps (state of ES-MDP); no versioning, rollback or dedup/merge of content
signatures.later_use: Cache entries scored for every later query in Phase II
signatures.claimed_effect: Library grows to ~50-80 skills before Phase II and specializes (App.E.2); ablation without O_{G+1} lowers AIME24 56.4->55.0
signatures.failure_boundary: Duplicate/conflicting skills never merged; evaluation-time library state unspecified; math-only

signatures.object: Skill selection/injection read path (not a separate learned retriever)
signatures.information: Query and cache skill texts (truncated to 128 tokens); policy conditional log-prob s_k
signatures.operation: softmax(s_k/sigma) with epsilon-greedy (0.1) and confidence gate delta=0.35; selected skill prepended with 'SKILL:' prefix
signatures.output: Skill-conditioned rollouts (73% utilization) or unaided rollouts
signatures.feedback: Hierarchical reward gives correct-with-skill advantage over correct-unaided
signatures.selection_rule_data: Selection draw z_t has no loss term in Eq.6; bonus shapes worker's use of injected skills, not an explicitly credited selection action
signatures.persistence: Not persistent per se; depends on S1 library and on policy weights
signatures.later_use: Every Phase II rollout and evaluation
signatures.claimed_effect: Policy gradient directly shapes selection; random selection ablation 55.1 vs 56.4 AIME24
signatures.failure_boundary: Low delta over-injects (89% use, -1.2 AIME24); high delta suppresses use

signatures.object: Model weights trained with GRPO jointly with S1/S2 (boundary component, not itself the retained harness object)
signatures.information: Group-relative advantages over G=8 rollouts with DAPO dynamic sampling
signatures.operation: 500-step warm-up with binary reward, then 1,500 steps with skill-augmented hierarchical reward
signatures.output: Policy that conditions on SKILL: prefix
signatures.claimed_effect: +1.8~3.5 points over GRPO on 7 benchmarks across 2 backbones
signatures.failure_boundary: Gain for binary-reward variant is ~0.6 AIME24 over GRPO (E021)

gap.author_gap: Skill selection/summarization is delegated to an external retriever decoupled from the policy gradient, and the library is updated independently of the RL objective (E002, E003).
gap.checked_gap: Real but narrower: neighbours EvolveR, SkillRL and Wang-2025 SAGE already move skills into the training loop (E015, E016); the residual is policy-driven (log-prob) selection and a reward bonus for skill use. Whether decoupling from an external retriever is the binding bottleneck is not tested (no embedding-retriever + same RL control).

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: retrieved reference substrate as conditioning input read by the model. rsi: skill library injected into rollouts the policy is trained on, with library built from same rollouts.
pattern_mapping.required_conditions_differences: RS requires category holdout and cheap baselines; rsi H28 requires lever ablation (context-only/weights-only/coupled) and clean split; neither is satisfied here.

expectations.reason: Skill generation uses the positive traces of the same GRPO group that updates the weights (App.A.2 steps 4-9).
Skill text is declarative guidance, weights procedural, but roles are not separated experimentally (no context-only vs weights-only vs coupled arms).
Policy trained on SKILL:-prefixed prompts; library revised only from successes (tau+), not diagnosed failures.
Failure avoided: the policy is trained on the injected artifact, not a recall bank beside it.
Whether the library freezes at test time and whether the adaptation stream differs from reported benchmarks is not stated.
No context-only / weights-only / coupled arms with seeds; only GRPO baseline and three single-run ablations.
Plateau of context-only adaptation and sample-inefficiency of weights-only RL are not demonstrated as motivation.
Add/Update(utility)/Evict/Load/Delete with caps; no content merge, conflict resolution or dedup.
Admission is a format-validation pipeline; no execution/marginal-gain test before an entry can be selected.
Selection is a log-prob retrieval score; learning-by-gradient is asserted (E004) but not carried by the loss (E005).
Eviction uses raw reward EMA, no memory-on/off counterfactual; authors admit utility is difficulty-confounded and IG results are not reported.
Selection and skill-generation tokens receive no advantage in Eq.6; only worker tokens are optimized.
Random-selection and frozen-seed-library ablations exist (single run); no skill-off-at-inference test of the trained policy.
No overlap analysis between DeepScaleR sources and the declared OOD Omni-MATH set.
No embedding-retriever or longer-context baseline under the same RL budget; compared methods are different re-implemented systems.
Gate, epsilon, cache size and warm-up sensitivity given, on AIME24 only; no library-coverage analysis.
'Same computational budget' stated but undefined; ARISE costs +16.6% per step (reported) and +3% tokens.

claims.text: ARISE+GRPO beats vanilla GRPO family and memory-augmented baselines on AMC23/AIME24/25 and Omni-MATH for two backbones.
claims.setting: DeepScaleR (~40K) training, 2,000 steps, G=8; Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 and Phi-4-mini; Pass@1 greedy x32
claims.baseline_control: GRPO, Dr.GRPO, DAPO, GSPO, EvolveR+GRPO, SimpleMem+GRPO (adapted); SkillRL named but not tabulated
claims.selection_vs_test: Train DeepScaleR; test AMC23/AIME24/25/Omni-MATH; hyperparameter sweep on AIME24 (a test set)
claims.result_denominator: Single reported numbers; Qwen3-4B: +2.5/+2.3/+1.8 competition, +2.9 Omni vs GRPO; Phi-4: +2.6/+2.3/+1.2, +2.0
claims.allowed_conclusion: In single-number results, ARISE+GRPO is about 2-3 points above vanilla GRPO and 0.9-1.3 above the best GRPO variant on the Omni-MATH average, but is not best in 3 of 16 cells despite the text saying so; effects are unreplicated and small for 30-problem AIME sets.

claims.text: The policy gradient directly shapes skill selection end-to-end, so the library and policy co-evolve.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Not supported as stated: Eq.6 has no selection/generation term; co-movement of library size and accuracy is correlational.

claims.text: Each component (hierarchical reward, policy selection, skill-generation rollout, confidence gate) contributes.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Ablation deltas of 0.4-2.3 points point the same way but are unreplicated; binary-reward variant is only ~0.6 above GRPO on AIME24.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Reported single-run gains of about 2-3 points over GRPO on olympiad math with a self-built skill library retained across training; ablations suggest hierarchical reward, skill generation and policy-scored selection each add ~1-2 points.
assessment.unresolved: Library vs reward-shaping vs extra-prompt attribution; end-to-end selection learning; test-time library state; Omni-MATH overlap; variance; nearest neighbours not compared.

G.reason: Real limitation (external retriever, independent library update) with neighbours named, but nearest neighbours (Wang-2025 SAGE, SkillRL) are not compared and decoupling is not shown to be the bottleneck.

M.reason: Concrete manager/worker mechanism and reward design, but the key assumption that the policy gradient shapes selection/generation is not carried by the written objective (Eq.6 covers worker tokens only); utility is difficulty-confounded by the authors' own account.

X.reason: Read path, write path, five lifecycle operations, validation pipeline and hyperparameters are reconstructable; admission is format-only, no versioning/rollback/dedup, and eval-time library state is unstated.

E.measurement.reason: Exact-match / symbolic-equivalence verifiers on AMC/AIME/Omni-MATH are trustworthy; reporting slips do not change the metric (24 vs 5 seed skills; AIME25 49.1 in ablation vs 48.3 in Table 1; text says best everywhere but 3 cells are not).

E.causality.reason: Relevant ablations exist (binary reward, random selection, no O_{G+1}, no gate) but are single-run, no external-retriever control, no skill-off inference test, binary-reward variant barely beats GRPO, compute/prompt-length confounds only partly addressed.

E.holdout.reason: Test sets are distinct from training pools, but hyperparameters appear tuned on AIME24 with no validation split, 'OOD' Omni-MATH has no overlap audit, and test-time library state is unspecified.

E.statistics.reason: Counts and several negative cells are reported, but no std/CI or training-seed variation; 32 greedy runs are non-independent (A2 ladder level 1).

E.cost.reason: Per-step wall-clock (+16.6%) with breakdown and token overhead (+3.0%) are reported; budget-matching unit for baselines is undefined.
